title: Spiral galaxy NGC 1097
caption: The spiral galaxy NGC 1097, imaged by ESO's Very Large Telescope
celestial: NGC 1097 · constellation Fornax · about 60 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: This nearly true-color view shows the spiral galaxy NGC 1097, about 60 million light-years away in the constellation Fornax. It was made with the VIMOS instrument on Melipal, the 8.2-meter Unit Telescope 3, part of ESO's Very Large Telescope.

Three wavebands were used, with R-band shown as red, V as green and B as blue. Because the colors follow the order of the wavelengths, the result is close to what our eyes would perceive, only far deeper. Observing conditions were very good, with seeing, the blurring caused by the atmosphere, well below 1 arcsecond.

The images were taken on the night of 9 to 10 December 2004, with Chile's President Ricardo Lagos present at the observatory. Exposure times were short, at 2.25 minutes in R, 3 in V and 6 in B. Astronomers from ESO's Paranal science operations took and pre-processed all the exposures, and the image covers 7.7 by 6.6 arcminutes of sky.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (6.85 x 7.74 arcminutes) and distance (60 million light years), the frame spans roughly 120,000 × 135,000 light-years. Its light set out about 60 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: VIMOS recorded R-band light (shown red), V-band light (green) and B-band light (blue), giving an almost-true color composite.
